Not the typeset journal version of record (DOI 10.1016/j.chbah.2026.100289). arXiv v1 had a different title ('Using Generative AI Personas Increases Collective Diversity in Human Ideation').
source.title_on_document: Diverse AI Personas Can Mitigate the Homogenization Effect in Human-AI Collaborative Ideation

supplement.where: Supplementary Materials appended to the same PDF, pp. 28-53
supplement.holds: Persona taxonomy, persona descriptions and prompts (pp. 29-38); Table S1 per-persona similarity (p. 39); Figures S1-S3 (pp. 40-42); participant protocol and interface screenshots for each condition (pp. 43-51); Table S2 Bayesian model results, equivalence tests and Bayes factors (pp. 52-53); Table S3 power analysis with story-level arm means and Cohen's d (p. 53). The main-text statistics (Tables 2-6) are all in the main text.

paper_design_summary: Phase 1 prompted GPT-4o with 10 AI personas to produce 300 three-sentence plot ideas for an adventure story on another planet and compared their embedding similarity within and across personas (model-only). In Phase 2, 100 UK Prolific workers were randomly assigned to write an eight-sentence story with no AI (0-plot), with the option to request one persona-generated plot (1-plot), or with the option to request up to five (5-plot); plots were drawn at random from the 300-plot pool. Diversity across writers was scored with text-embedding-ada-002 cosine similarity (to the condition centroid and pairwise), and stories were also compared on NLTK linguistic counts.

studies.label: Phase 1: diversity of 300 plot ideas from 10 GPT-4o personas (model-only)

assignment.what_was_assigned: No people. Ten personas each generated 30 plots; a benchmark of 30 plots used the Doshi and Hauser (2024) prompt.

participants.who: No human participants. 300 persona plots plus 30 benchmark plots.

ai_tool.name_model: Personas built with ChatGPT o1-preview; plots generated with GPT-4o (version 2024-05-13, temperature 0.9, top P 1) on Azure OpenAI; benchmark plots with GPT-4 on the Azure OpenAI chat playground
ai_tool.how_used: AI generated all plot ideas; no human use.

task.description: Three-sentence plot ideas for an adventure story on another planet

studies.label: Phase 2: story writing with or without persona-generated plot ideas (Prolific)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Condition: 0-plot (no AI), 1-plot (option to request one AI plot idea), 5-plot (option to request up to five AI plot ideas)
assignment.quote: The participants were randomly assigned to write an eight-sentence short story under one of three experimental conditions
assignment.locator: p. 10, Section 3.1; also p. 43 (Supplementary Materials, Story writing by participants)

arms.name: 0-plot
arms.description: Control: write the story with no AI support. Followed by a question whether the participant used ChatGPT or a similar tool.

arms.name: 1-plot
arms.description: Option to click a button to receive one AI plot idea, drawn at random from the 300 persona plots; free to use or disregard it.

arms.name: 5-plot
arms.description: Option to request up to five AI plot ideas (five Idea buttons), drawn at random from the 300 persona plots; free to use or disregard them.

participants.exclusions: Three participants in the 0-plot control group were excluded because they reported using external AI to inspire their stories. Per-arm counts at assignment are not stated.
participants.who: Prolific workers based in the UK, approval rating at or above 95 percent, between 100 and 1,000,000 prior submissions (same criteria as Doshi and Hauser 2024); paid 3 pounds for about 15-20 minutes
participants.quote: we recruited 100 human participants using the online platform Prolific ... we analyzed 97 stories: 32 in the control group, 33 in the 1-plot condition, and 32 in the 5-plot condition.
participants.locator: p. 10-11, Section 3.1; Table 3, p. 13 (counts 32/33/32); p. 44 (payment and duration)

ai_tool.name_model: Pre-generated plots from GPT-4o (version 2024-05-13) prompted with 10 personas built with o1-preview; no live model interaction by participants
ai_tool.how_used: In the AI arms, participants could click a button to receive a three-sentence plot idea (one in 1-plot, up to five in 5-plot) chosen at random from the 300-plot persona pool. Requesting and using plots was optional. The paper does not report how many participants requested plots.

task.description: Write an exactly eight-sentence story about an adventure on another planet for a teenage and young adult audience. The consent page also mentions a prior task of providing ten words, which the paper does not analyze.
task.duration: About 15-20 minutes for the whole study (consent page, p. 44)

outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Cosine similarity (scaled x100) between each story's text-embedding-ada-002 embedding and the mean embedding of all stories in the same condition. Higher = more homogeneous. Analyzed by OLS with control as reference (Table 2) and one-way ANOVA on means (Table 3).

diversity_detail.metric: Cosine similarity (x100) of each story to its condition centroid
diversity_detail.computed_over: Each story against the centroid (mean embedding) of all stories in its condition
diversity_detail.uncertainty: OLS regression of story-level centroid similarity on condition dummies (conventional SEs, n = 97); one-way ANOVA across the three conditions
diversity_detail.notes: Higher similarity = less diverse. Table 2 reproduces Doshi and Hauser (2024) Table S11 coefficients for comparison.

outcomes.name: Pairwise cosine similarity between stories within a condition
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Cosine similarity (x100) of text-embedding-ada-002 embeddings for every pair of stories in the same condition. Main model: mixed-effects regression similarity ~ condition + (1|story1_id) + (1|story2_id), REML, 1,520 pairs (Table 4). Robustness variants of the same outcome: one-way ANOVA, pairwise t-tests, and a 10,000-iteration permutation test on each story's average similarity to the other stories in its condition (97 stories); a Bayesian hierarchical model (Table S2). Higher = more homogeneous.

contrasts.reported: Mixed model: Baseline (Control: 0-plot) 82.699 (SE 0.327); 1-plot effect -1.073, SE 0.458, z = -2.341, p = 0.019, 95% CI [-1.971, -0.175]; story-level variance 2.765 (0.212); residual variance 5.45. Story-level robustness: ANOVA F(2, 94) = 2.33, p = 0.103; 0-plot vs 1-plot t = 1.88, p = 0.064; permutation p = 0.113. Bayesian: condition[1-plot] -0.882 (sd 0.419), 95% HDI [-1.686, -0.042]; BF01 = 0.548. Cohen's d = 0.467 (0-plot vs 1-plot). Table S3 story-level means: 1-plot 81.74 vs control 82.62. Lower similarity = more diverse.
contrasts.locator: p. 13-14, Section 3.3.2 and Table 4; p. 14-15 (Bayesian, power); p. 52, Table S2; p. 53, Table S3

contrasts.reported: Mixed model: 5-plot effect -0.488, SE 0.462, z = -1.056, p = 0.291, 95% CI [-1.394, 0.418]. Story-level: 0-plot vs 5-plot t = 1.45, p = 0.151. Bayesian: condition[5-plot] -0.625 (sd 0.433), 95% HDI [-1.486, 0.203]; BF01 = 1.724. Cohen's d = 0.363. Table S3 story-level means: 5-plot 82.00 vs control 82.62.
contrasts.locator: p. 13-14, Section 3.3.2 and Table 4; p. 14-15; p. 52, Table S2; p. 53, Table S3

contrasts.reported: Story-level: 1-plot versus 5-plot t = -0.73, p = 0.470. Bayesian 5-plot vs 1-plot: mean difference 0.258, 95% HDI [-0.594, 1.080], P(effect in ROPE) 0.682, BF01 = 3.968. Cohen's d = -0.180 (1-plot vs 5-plot).
contrasts.locator: p. 14-15, Section 3.3.2; p. 52-53, Tables S2 and S3

diversity_detail.metric: Pairwise cosine similarity (x100) between stories in the same condition
diversity_detail.computed_over: All pairs of stories within a condition (496 pairs 0-plot, 528 pairs 1-plot, 496 pairs 5-plot); robustness check uses each story's mean similarity to all other stories in its condition
diversity_detail.uncertainty: Mixed-effects model with crossed random intercepts for the two stories in each pair (REML); robustness: ANOVA and t-tests on 97 story-level averages, permutation test (10,000 iterations); Bayesian hierarchical model (4 chains x 2,000 iterations)
diversity_detail.notes: Lower similarity = more diverse. The paper prints two different overall F values for the story-level analysis: F(2, 94) = 2.33, p = 0.103 (p. 13) and Observed F = 2.720 (Table S3, p. 53).

sample_overlap.quote: Table 2 ... Comparison of Regression Results of Our Modified Experiment to Doshi and Hauser (2024)'s as Reported in Their Supplementary Materials, Table S11
sample_overlap.locator: p. 12, Table 2. New participants recruited on Prolific with Doshi and Hauser's (2024) criteria and protocol (p. 10, p. 43); Doshi and Hauser's coefficients are printed only for comparison, no participants are shared.

eligibility.reason: Study S2 randomly assigned 100 Prolific participants to no AI or to optional access to one or five AI-generated plot ideas (p. 10); 97 analyzed (32/33/32, p. 11). Outcomes are embedding-based diversity of the stories across writers (Tables 2-4) and NLTK counts on the stories (Tables 5-6). No human-rated creativity outcome. Phase 1 (S1) is model-only.

one_line_finding: Among 97 UK Prolific writers, optional access to one persona-generated AI plot lowered pairwise story similarity versus no AI (mixed model -1.073, 95% CI [-1.971, -0.175], p = 0.019, Table 4, p. 14), while the 5-plot arm (-0.488, p = 0.291) and the centroid-similarity regression (1-plot -0.493, 5-plot -0.356, Table 2, p. 12) showed no significant difference.
open_questions: Group sizes for the linguistic comparisons (Tables 5-6, p. 16) are not printed. Some printed human-only means are not multiples of 1/32 (e.g., named characters 0.634, a count variable), so the human-only group may not be the 32 analyzed control stories; a check by the auditor whether Tables 5-6 group stories by assigned condition (32 vs 65) or by some other split is warranted. Table S3 (p. 53) labels its means 'Intent-to-Treat Analysis: Originally Assigned Conditions', which suggests some analysis used a different grouping, but the paper does not say which.
The story-level ANOVA is reported as F(2, 94) = 2.33, p = 0.103 in the text (p. 13) and as Observed F = 2.720 in Table S3 (p. 53).

Mixed-model control baseline is 82.699 (Table 4) while Table S3 gives the control story-level mean as 82.62 and the Bayesian intercept is 82.616 (Table S2); these come from different models, but the auditor may wish to confirm which baseline to record.
The AI arms offered optional access to plots. The paper does not report how many participants in the 1-plot and 5-plot arms requested or used a plot, so the contrasts are effects of offered access.
Table 2 prints standard errors to one decimal place (0.5, 0.5, 0.3); exact SEs for the centroid regression are not given.
Which of the three diversity analyses the authors treat as primary is not stated; Section 3.2 calls them complementary, and the story-level analysis is labeled a robustness check (p. 11, p. 13).
notes: Direction fields for S2-O1 and S2-O2 refer to the printed similarity measure: 'treatment_lower' means lower similarity, i.e., more diverse stories in the AI arm (sign reversed relative to the codebook's diversity convention). Comparison 1-plot or 5-plot vs 0-plot is coded ai_vs_bau because the control had no AI; the AI input itself is the persona-diversified configuration the paper proposes, and the paper's contrast with uniform-prompt AI is only through Doshi and Hauser's (2024) separate sample (Table 2). Phase 1 compares 300 persona plots: mean intra-persona similarity 87.41 +/- 3.17 vs inter-persona 82.93 +/- 3.12, t = 119.9443, Cohen's d = 1.4254 (Table 1, p. 7); 30 plots from the Doshi and Hauser prompt had intra-group similarity 90.99 (SD 2.78) (p. 7; Table S1, p. 39). Phase 1 has no human participants and no outcome on the three questions. Data: the paper says the full list of plots is available from the corresponding author (p. 31, Supplementary Materials); no data or code URL is given. The paper's power analysis reports 55.4 percent achieved power and 165 participants needed for 80 percent power (p. 15; Table S3, p. 53).
